newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Red October to issue shares.
newsitem.headline: Russian Red October to issue shares.

text.p: Russia's biggest confectioner OAO Red October plans to issue preferred shares through a private placement in April or May this year, the company's president Anatoly Daursky said on Tuesday.

"We have been in a hurry with our shareholders' meeting and with the audit due to our preferred shares issue," Daursky told a news conference. "June and July will be a dead season, but April or May will be right for the launch."

The Red October shareholders' meeting on April 12 approved an issue of about 1.48 million preferred shares, to be sold at 75-80 percent of the market value of ordinary shares at the time of placement, the company said in a statement. It is Red October's first issue of preferred shares.
On the Russian Trading System, a local version of NASDAQ, Red October was last traded at $20.0 on April 11.
Brunswick is the company's lead manager on the issue.
The company raised the 1996 dividend on ordinary shares to 1,900 roubles from 1,800 roubles in 1,800.
Currently Red October's single biggest shareholder is the Moscow government with 19.7 percent of shares. Foreign companies own 31.7 percent.
